memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "to serve as a sign among you. In the future, when your children ask you, 'What do these stones mean?' tell them that the flow of the Jordan was cut off before the ark of the covenant of the Lord. When it crossed the Jordan, the waters of the Jordan were cut off. These stones are to be a memorial to the people of Israel forever." — Josh 4:6-7 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Here is the purpose of the stones spelled out plainly: they were to spark questions from the next generation. "When your children ask, 'What do these stones mean?'" — that was exactly the point. The memorial was designed to open the door to telling the story of God's faithfulness to the young.

This is one of the most beautiful responsibilities God gives His people: passing faith on to our children. God does not intend that each generation start from scratch. The stones stood there precisely so that curious children would ask, and parents would answer by telling of the mighty works of God.

Notice the pattern. The children see something unusual, they ask, and the parents explain. God builds curiosity into the way faith is handed down. Our task is to live and mark our lives in such a way that the next generation wonders and asks — and then to be ready with the story of what God has done.

The New Testament carries this same heart, urging us to bring up children in the instruction of the Lord (Eph 6:4) and to declare God's works to those who come after us (Ps 78:4). Every generation needs to hear afresh of God's saving power, ultimately fulfilled in Christ. May our lives be full of "stones" that make the young ask, "What does this mean?"

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you living in a way that prompts younger ones to ask about your faith?
2. What "story of God's faithfulness" do you need to pass on to the next generation?
3. When a child asks about God, are you ready and eager to answer?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, help me leave markers of Your faithfulness that make the next generation curious. Give me a ready heart to tell them what You have done. Amen.
